title: How to order prawn noodle like a Singaporean
title_zh: 新加坡虾面怎么点才地道
summary: Soup or dry, pick your noodle, and how a local orders it. Plus the free soup top-up most stalls give.
alt: Pocket Local guide slide: how to order prawn noodle in Singapore
sections: First · Soup or dry?
Dry comes tossed in chilli sauce or ketchup, with the soup on the side. Either way, the rich prawn broth is the whole point.
Then · Pick your noodle
Thick yellow noodle, bee hoon, or kuey tiao (the flat white noodle). You can mix, e.g. bee hoon + noodle.
My order
Dry, yellow noodle / bee hoon, no chilli, no bean sprouts. That's my taste. Most Singaporeans like chilli.
Tip · Soup top-up
Most stalls will top up your soup once. Ask more than once and you might get a stare.
Where to go
You'll find a good one at most hawker centres.

title: Free: 1 day in Singapore with kids
title_zh: 免费：带孩子玩新加坡一日行程
summary: Colourful Katong in the morning, a break from the heat, then satay and two free light shows at night.
alt: Pocket Local guide slide: free 1-day Singapore plan for families
sections: Morning: Katong & Joo Chiat
Take the brown line to Marine Parade. See the colourful Peranakan shophouses, try nyonya kueh, then Katong laksa for lunch.
1:30pm: hide from the heat
Early afternoon is the hottest part of the day. Head to an aircon mall or back to the hotel for a nap or the pool.
Evening: satay & two free light shows
Dinner at Lau Pa Sat, blue line 1 stop to Bayfront, Spectra at Marina Bay Sands, then the Supertree light show at Gardens by the Bay.
Get the full plan
The full plan has times, MRT lines and little local tips. Download it free at pocketlocalsg.com/free, or comment PLAN on Instagram.

title: Singapore with young kids: 5 things I wish someone told me
title_zh: 带小孩玩新加坡，5个过来人建议
summary: From a local dad who took his two boys around the world. Save this for your trip.
alt: Pocket Local guide slide: Singapore with young kids, 5 tips
sections: 1. Go out early or late
Plan outdoor stuff before 11am or after 5pm. The midday sun is no joke.
2. Malls are your rest stops
Clean toilets, baby rooms and food courts. Use them to recharge.
3. Hawker centres love kids
Loud, casual, nobody minds the noise. Easy, cheap, tasty.
4. Rain comes and goes fast
Wait 30 to 60 minutes in a mall and carry on with your day.
5. Don't pack the day too full
One area in the morning, one in the evening. That's enough.

title: Where locals actually eat
title_zh: 本地人真正吃饭的地方
summary: Skip the tourist food halls. Neighbourhood malls have big aircon food courts, right next to the MRT.
alt: Pocket Local guide slide: where locals actually eat
sections: AMK Hub · Red line, Ang Mo Kio
Right next to Ang Mo Kio MRT. Big food court, real heartland vibe, and you pay what locals pay.
Jurong Point · Green line, Boon Lay
One of the biggest neighbourhood malls in the west, connected to Boon Lay MRT. Lots to eat, all aircon.
City Square Mall · Purple line, Farrer Park
Connected to Farrer Park MRT, near Little India. An easy stop for lunch after walking around Little India.
Why go?
Aircon so no sweating in the heat, local prices instead of tourist prices, right next to the station, and it's where Singaporeans eat every day.

title: One easy evening in Marina Bay
summary: Satay at Lau Pa Sat, the blue line 1 stop to Bayfront, then two free light shows. Kid friendly, no rushing.
alt: Pocket Local guide slide: one easy evening in Marina Bay
sections: 7:00pm · Satay at Lau Pa Sat

The road beside Lau Pa Sat closes at night and the satay stalls come out. Get chicken and mutton, plus rice cakes (ketupat) for the kids. Lots of stalls will try to get your business. Honestly, they're all just as good. If it's packed, go with them and they'll find you a table. If not, just grab your own, no pressure.
After dinner · Blue line, 1 stop

From Downtown MRT, take the blue line one stop to Bayfront. That's Marina Bay Sands. Walking there takes about 25 minutes, not fun with tired kids. Just tap your bank card at the gantry, no need to buy a ticket.
8pm or 9pm · Spectra at Marina Bay Sands

A free light, water and music show over the bay, about 15 minutes. Sit on the steps at the Event Plaza in front of MBS. There are shows at 8pm and 9pm, so if the kids eat slowly, no need to rush. Just catch the 9pm one.
8:45pm · Supertree lights at Gardens by the Bay

Walk through MBS to the Supertree Grove (around 15 minutes). Lie down on the ground and look up. Free, and kids love it. This works if you caught the 8pm Spectra. Went for 9pm? Save the Supertrees for another night.

title: Meet Pocket Local, your local friend in Singapore
summary: Who I am, why I started Pocket Local, and how I plan your Singapore trip.
sections: Everywhere we travelled, locals looked after us
My family travelled to many countries, and everywhere we went, local people helped us and looked after us. Now it's my turn, so I started Pocket Local.
What I do

Tell me about your trip: dates, who's coming and what you love. I build your plan day by day, with maps and food picks. Then I'm on WhatsApp the whole trip. Not a tour: you explore freely, and you book your own hotel and tickets.
Planned around you
A sample plan: Day 1, arrive and settle in. Day 2, hawker breakfast and the hidden gems most tourists miss. Day 3 at your own pace, with kids, parents and budget all planned in. English and 中文.

title: Half a day in Katong & Joo Chiat
title_zh: 加东与如切 · 半日游
summary: Colourful shophouses, Katong laksa and nyonya kueh. A side of Singapore most tourists miss.
alt: Pocket Local guide slide: half a day in Katong and Joo Chiat
sections: Morning · The colourful houses
Peranakan shophouses along Koon Seng Road and Joo Chiat Road. Go in the morning when it's cooler, great for family photos.
Lunch · Katong laksa
Short rice noodles in spicy coconut broth, cut short so you eat it with just a spoon.
Snack · Nyonya kueh
Colourful Peranakan cakes. Get a mix to share, kids always go for the rainbow ones.
Getting there · Brown line, Marine Parade

You come out at Marine Parade Central, a real local neighbourhood with a hawker centre. Then cross the road into Katong. Too hot or raining? Parkway Parade mall is right there for air-con and shelter.
